about: What the widget and its host say to each other (ADR 0034; docs/sdks/PLAN.md). Every implementation keeps its own copy, and its tests hold that copy to this file and to fixtures.json: change the protocol here first.

ready.version: integer: the protocol the widget speaks; a widget that sends none speaks version 0

error.code: string: one of errors.known, or any other code

open-url.url: string (version 1, to an app only): an http or https address that leaves the widget, which the app opens outside it

identify.token: string: an identity token the host's server signed; or null (version 1): the host has nobody signed in

navigate.path: string (version 1): a path under /widget, with its query

channels.about: How the widget speaks to its host, which it finds once, when it starts, in this order: the page that frames it, else the app whose bridge object is in its page. An app's bridge carries the protocol's messages as JSON text; a frame's, as objects.

frame.toHost: postMessage on the frame's parent: an object
frame.toWidget: a message event from the parent itself, from an origin the workspace allows (any while it names none, from the page on top only)

ios.toWidget: window.postMessage(message, the portal's origin), run by the app in the page's own world: an object

android.toHost: the bridge's postMessage (WebViewCompat.addWebMessageListener's object, in the portal's origin alone): JSON text
android.toWidget: the bridge's onmessage, from the reply proxy of the widget's messages: JSON text

react-native.toWidget: window.postMessage(message, the portal's origin), injected by the app: an object

errors.about: Any other code means the widget couldn't take the request at the time.

settings.portal_url: string: the portal's canonical address, which messages count from
settings.accent: { color, foreground } (#rrggbb each): the widget's color, else the portal's, and the text that reads on it; or null for the portal's own colors
settings.position: left or right: the side of the page the launcher sits on
settings.theme: system, light or dark: the portal's look
settings.language: the reader's language, one of the seven
settings.labels: { open, close, loading }: the launcher's words, in that language
